mainTopic: Breaking the מנחה into pieces (פתיתה), and the ברכה on small pieces of bread
overview: The amud opens with רבה finishing the earlier discussion. He says the מנחת מאפה is the offering that needs two exclusions. A new משנה then teaches how a מנחה is folded and broken. For a regular person's מנחה, the כהן folds it into four and separates the pieces. For the מנחת כהנים, he folds it but does not separate the pieces. For the מנחת כהן משיח, he does not fold it at all. רבי שמעון says the כהן offerings are not broken at all, because no קמיצה is taken from them. Every broken offering is broken into olive-sized pieces. A ברייתא learns these rules from the פסוק, and רבה answers that the כהן משיח's offering is folded into two but not into four. רב יוסף uses the olive-sized pieces to rule that bread pieces of a כזית get המוציא and smaller pieces get מזונות. אביי challenges him and the גמרא goes back and forth over this. The final ruling is רב ששת's: even crumbs smaller than a כזית get המוציא. רבא adds that this is only when the crumbs still look like bread.

steps.title: רבה: the baked offering is the one that needs two exclusions
steps.stepSummary: רבה finishes the earlier discussion: the מנחת מאפה is the offering that needs two exclusions from pouring oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: Which item needs two exclusions? You must say it is the oven-baked meal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה closes the previous discussion about which offerings get oil poured on them (יציקה). He says the oven-baked offering is the one that needs two separate exclusions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two limiting phrases. רבה says both are needed for the מנחת מאפה, because it comes in two kinds: loaves (חלות) and wafers (רקיקין). So both kinds are left out of pouring, while the מנחת כהנים is not left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Exclusions: words in a פסוק that limit a law and leave something out
You must say: there is only one possible answer
The oven-baked meal offering, which comes as loaves or as wafers

phrases.english: Rabba says:
What is the item that needs two exclusions?
phrases.notes: He means the two limiting phrases in the פסוק, "upon it" and "it is a מנחה," which were discussed just before this.

phrases.english: You must say: this is the oven-baked meal offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁצָּרִיךְ שְׁנֵי מִיעוּטִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion about יציקה from the previous part of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two exclusions in the פסוק both refer to the מנחת מאפה, because it has two kinds, loaves and wafers.

steps.title: The משנה: how each type of offering is folded
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives three rules: a regular person's מנחה is folded and separated, a כהן's מנחה is folded but not separated, and the כהן משיח's מנחה is not folded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The meal offering of an Israelite: he folds one into two and two into four, and separates. The meal offering of priests: he folds one into two and two into four, and does not separate. The meal offering of the anointed priest: he would not fold it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains how the כהן breaks a מנחה into pieces, and the rule depends on whose offering it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular Jew's מנחה, the כהן folds it in half, then in half again, and pulls the pieces apart. For a כהן's own מנחה he folds it the same way but does not pull the pieces apart. For the כהן גדול's daily offering (the כהן משיח), he does not fold it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He folds the baked offering, doubling it over
He separates the pieces at the folds
A מנחה brought by a regular כהן; it is burned completely
The anointed כהן גדול, who brings a daily griddle-cake offering

steps.confusionAlert: Folding (קיפול) and separating (הבדלה) are two different actions. The מנחת כהנים gets folded but not separated. Do not assume that folding always ends with the pieces pulled apart.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The meal offering of an Israelite: he folds one into two,
and two into four, and separates.
The meal offering of priests: he folds one into two,
and two into four, and does not separate.

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ – לֹא הָיָה מְקַפְּלָה.
phrases.english: The meal offering of the anointed priest: he would not fold it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, the breaking of the מנחה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Israelite: fold into four and separate. Priests: fold into four, no separating. Anointed priest: no folding.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: offerings with no handful are not broken at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the מנחת כהנים and the מנחת כהן משיח are not broken at all, because no קמיצה is taken from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: The meal offering of priests and the meal offering of the anointed priest have no breaking, because they have no removal of a handful. Any offering with no handful removed has no breaking.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה. He says neither of the two כהן offerings is broken at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He links the two actions together: breaking happens only on offerings that have a קמיצה. The כהן offerings are burned completely, so no קמיצה is taken from them. That is why, in his view, they are not broken either.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the baked offering into pieces
Taking a handful from the מנחה to burn on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי שמעון makes breaking depend on קמיצה. The first opinion in the משנה does not, since it requires folding even for the מנחת כהנים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The meal offering of priests and the meal offering of the anointed priest
have no breaking,
because they have no removal of a handful,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן קְמִיצָה – אֵין בָּהֶן פְּתִיתָה.
phrases.english: and any offering with no handful removed has no breaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's rules for the כהן offerings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no breaking without קמיצה, so the כהן offerings are not broken.

steps.title: All broken offerings are broken into olive-sized pieces
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by giving the size of the pieces: each is the size of an olive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them, he breaks into olive-sized pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by telling us how big each broken piece should be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever offerings do get broken, the pieces must be the size of a כזית. This sets the size for every case of breaking.

keyTerms.meaning: Pieces the size of an olive (a כזית each)
He breaks them into pieces

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three folding rules (Israelite, priests, anointed priest). רבי שמעון says the כהן offerings are not broken at all. Every broken piece is a כזית.

phrases.english: And all of them, he breaks into olive-sized pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the משנה with the size of the pieces
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every broken offering is broken into olive-sized pieces.

steps.title: The verse says pieces, so more than two
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word "פתים" that the offering is broken into more than two pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "Break it" — might it be only into two? The verse says "pieces."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns the breaking rules from the פסוק. First it shows the offering must be broken into more than two pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "פתות" alone could mean breaking it just once, into two. The extra word "פתים" (pieces) shows that each half is broken again.

keyTerms.meaning: Break it, the first word of the פסוק
Pieces
One might have thought
Therefore the פסוק says

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
"Break it" — one might think only into two?
The verse says "pieces."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for the folding rules of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking means more than two pieces.

steps.title: The word "it" means not down to crumbs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word "אותה" that the pieces are not broken again into crumbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: If "pieces," might he turn it into crumbs? The verse says "it": break it into pieces, and not its pieces into pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now sets a limit on the breaking. It must not go so far that the offering turns into crumbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Pieces" could suggest breaking again and again with no end. The word "אותה" (it) means you break the whole offering into pieces, but you do not take those pieces and break them further.

keyTerms.meaning: Crumbs
"It," meaning the offering itself and not its pieces

phrases.english: If "pieces," one might think he should make it into crumbs?
The verse says "it":
it into pieces,
and not its pieces into pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the previous derivation so the breaking does not go on forever
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Break the offering into pieces, but do not break the pieces again.

steps.title: How the breaking works in practice
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא puts the rules into practice: the Israelite's offering is folded into four and separated, and the offerings of the כהנים and the כהן משיח are folded.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? The meal offering of an Israelite: he folds one into two and two into four and separates. The meal offering of priests and the anointed priest: he would fold it, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how its derivation is carried out. Notice that it says the offering of the כהן משיח is also folded. This sets up the next step's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule for the Israelite matches the משנה exactly. But the ברייתא groups the כהן משיח together with the כהנים as offerings that are folded. The משנה said the כהן משיח's offering is not folded at all.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? It introduces how a rule is carried out
Etc.: the quoted text continues

phrases.english: How so?
The meal offering of an Israelite: he folds one into two
and two into four and separates.
The meal offering of priests and the anointed priest:
he would fold it, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." means the ברייתא goes on. The key point is that it counts the כהן משיח among those who fold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the derivation from the פסוק to each type of offering
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the offering of the כהן משיח is folded.

steps.title: But the משנה said the anointed priest's offering is not folded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says the כהן משיח's offering is folded, when the משנה says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: He would not fold it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. The ברייתא says the כהן משיח's offering is folded, but our משנה says it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources seem to clash directly about the same offering. The גמרא now needs to explain how both can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely: it opens a challenge
He folds it

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the Mishna:
He would not fold it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 7 using the משנה in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the כהן משיח's offering is folded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה clearly says the כהן משיח's offering is not folded, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבה: folded into two, but not into four
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the כהן משיח's offering is folded once, into two. The משנה only means it is not folded into four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: He does not fold it into four, but he does fold it into two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה settles the contradiction. Each source is talking about a different amount of folding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the משנה says "he would not fold it," it means he does not do the full folding into four. The ברייתא's "he folds it" means one fold into two. So both sources are correct.

keyTerms.meaning: But: it introduces the part that is allowed
Into four

steps.whatToRemember: The מנחת כהן משיח is folded once into two, but not into four. This is how the משנה and the ברייתא fit together.

phrases.english: Rabba says:
He does not fold it into four,
but he does fold it into two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the meaning of folding: once into two versus fully into four
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה meant there is no folding at all, which would contradict the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה rules out folding into four, and the ברייתא allows folding into two, so they agree

steps.title: רבי שמעון: no breaking for the priests' offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: רבי שמעון says the מנחה of כהנים and of the כהן משיח are not broken into pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the meal offering of priests and the meal offering of the anointed priest have no breaking into pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of the משנה, where רבי שמעון says these two offerings are not broken at all. This sets up a new discussion based on the משנה's rule that broken pieces are olive-sized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned how each מנחה is folded and broken. רבי שמעון holds that the offerings of כהנים skip the breaking altogether. In the same passage, the משנה says all the offerings that are broken are broken into pieces the size of a כזית, and רב יוסף builds on that next.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the baked offering into pieces
A meal offering brought by an ordinary כהן
The anointed כהן גדול

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The meal offering of priests and the meal offering of the anointed priest
have no breaking into pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the folding discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the מנחות of כהנים and of the כהן משיח are not broken into pieces at all.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the blessing depends on olive-sized pieces
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a cooked dish with olive-sized bread pieces gets המוציא. If the pieces are smaller, it gets בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This cooked dish that has pieces of bread the size of an olive, we say "Who brings forth bread from the earth" on it. If it does not have olive-sized pieces, we say "Who creates various kinds of food" on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a practical rule about ברכות. Bread pieces in a cooked dish still count as bread if they are at least a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread that was broken up and cooked into a dish might lose its status as bread. רב יוסף draws the line at size. A כזית piece keeps the ברכה of המוציא, and smaller crumbs drop to בורא מיני מזונות.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooked dish with bread crumbs mixed in
Crumbs or broken pieces of bread
The size of an olive, a standard halachic measure
The ברכה said over bread
The ברכה said over grain foods that are not bread

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule for everyday ברכות over dishes made with bread pieces.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
This cooked dish that has in it
pieces of bread the size of an olive,
we recite over it
"Who brings forth bread from the earth";
if it does not have olive-sized pieces,
we recite over it "Who creates various kinds of food."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a practical ברכה rule on the משנה's olive-sized pieces.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread pieces of a כזית in a dish get המוציא. Smaller pieces get בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof from the meal offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one says המוציא before eating מנחות, and the משנה says the מנחות are broken into olive-sized pieces. So olive-sized pieces get המוציא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Where do I learn this from? A ברייתא teaches: if someone was standing and offering meal offerings in Jerusalem, he says "Blessed is He Who kept us alive and sustained us." When he took them to eat them, he says "Who brings forth bread from the earth." And the משנה taught: all of them are broken into olive-sized pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף proves his rule by putting two sources together. One source says the eater makes המוציא on the מנחה, and the other says its pieces are olive-sized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that a broken מנחה gets המוציא. The משנה tells us how big those pieces are, a כזית. Put together, olive-sized pieces of bread still count as bread for the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: "From where do I say this?" The speaker is about to bring a source for his own rule
The ברכה said on doing something new for the first time
Meal offerings made of flour

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: From where do I say this?
As a ברייתא teaches: if he was standing
and offering meal offerings in Jerusalem,
he says: "Blessed is He Who kept us alive and sustained us";
when he took them to eat them,
he says: "Who brings forth bread from the earth."
And the משנה taught: and all of them are broken into olive-sized pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב יוסף's rule.
steps.raayaObject: That olive-sized bread pieces get המוציא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that requires המוציא on מנחות, together with the משנה that says מנחות are broken into olive-sized pieces.

steps.title: אביי: what about the view that crushes them into flour?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks about the תנא of רבי ישמעאל's school, who says the pieces are crushed back into flour. Would he say no המוציא is made on the מנחה?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: And according to the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל, who said he crushes them until he turns them back into flour, would you also say that he does not recite "Who brings forth"?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's proof. According to another opinion, the מנחה pieces are much smaller than a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof depended on the pieces being olive-sized. The תנא of רבי ישמעאל's school says they are crushed into flour-like crumbs. The ברייתא still requires המוציא on the מנחה, so does that view really hold that tiny crumbs get no המוציא?

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher from רבי ישמעאל's study hall
He crushes them into crumbs
Their fine flour, the state they started in
"So too?" Would you say the same here?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And according to the תנא of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
who said he crushes them
until he turns them back into their flour,
would you also say that he does not recite "Who brings forth"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּלְתַנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule and his proof from the מנחה pieces.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If size decides the ברכה, the opinion that crushes the pieces into flour would have to say there is no המוציא on מנחות, which seems hard to accept.

steps.title: Crumbs still count as bread for חמץ and מצה
steps.stepSummary: If you answer that this view really says no המוציא, a ברייתא shows that a כזית gathered from the crumbs counts as bread. If it is חמץ, eating it on פסח carries כרת. If it is מצה, it fulfills the מצוה of מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say, yes, that is so, but a ברייתא teaches: if he gathered an olive-sized amount from all of them and ate it, if it is leavened, he is punished with כרת. If it is מצה, a person fulfills his obligation with them on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי blocks a possible way out. Tiny crumbs of a מנחה are still treated as full bread in other הלכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף might answer that, yes, that view makes no המוציא. אביי shows that the crumbs, once gathered into a כזית, are bread for חמץ and for מצה. So small size alone does not seem to take away a food's bread status, and רב יוסף's size rule is under pressure.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if you will say." The גמרא raises a possible answer in order to reject it
Punished with כרת, being cut off
Fulfilling one's obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the crumbs here are olive-sized pieces. Each crumb is tiny, and he gathers many of them together to make up a כזית.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף says olive-sized pieces get המוציא and smaller ones get מזונות. אביי questions this, since even tiny מנחה crumbs count as bread for חמץ and מצה.

phrases.english: And if you will say, yes, that is so,
but isn't it taught in a ברייתא: if he gathered from all of them
an olive-sized amount and ate it,
if it is leavened, he is punished with כרת;
phrases.notes: He means eating it on פסח, when חמץ is forbidden.

phrases.english: if it is מצה,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח.
phrases.english: a person fulfills his obligation with them on פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes off a possible answer to אביי's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that the crushed-flour view really makes no המוציא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats gathered crumbs as full bread for חמץ and מצה. So they should count as bread for המוציא too.

steps.title: The crumbs were pressed together
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about crumbs counting as bread is explained as a case where the crumbs were pressed into one mass.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where he pressed the crumbs together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge from step 14. It says the ברייתא is talking about crumbs that were squeezed together into one solid piece.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי wanted to prove that loose crumbs smaller than a כזית still count as bread. The answer limits the ברייתא to crumbs pressed into one piece. That piece is a full כזית, so the ברייתא proves nothing about loose small crumbs.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? This narrows a source to a specific case.
He pressed or kneaded them together into one mass.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
Where he pressed them together.
phrases.notes: He means the small crumbs were squeezed into one solid lump.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that loose crumbs smaller than a כזית count as bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about crumbs pressed into one piece, so it is not talking about loose small crumbs.

steps.title: The plural wording does not fit pressed crumbs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'he ate them' within the time of eating a פרס, which implies separate pieces, not one pressed mass.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at what is taught about it: 'And this is when he ate them within the time it takes to eat a פרס.' If they were pressed together, it should have said 'he ate it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 15 using the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'שאכלן,' in plural, and requires eating them within the time of eating a פרס. That fits many separate pieces eaten one after another. If the crumbs were pressed into one piece, the ברייתא should have said 'שאכלו,' in singular.

keyTerms.meaning: The time it takes to eat a half-loaf. Eating within this time joins small amounts into one act of eating.
It should have said.
If so.

steps.confusionAlert: The whole challenge hangs on one letter: שאכלן (them, plural) versus שאכלו (it, singular).

phrases.english: If so, that which is taught about it:
"And this is when he ate them"
"within the time of eating a half-loaf"
But if it is where he pressed them together,
it should have said "when he ate it"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 15 based on the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about crumbs pressed together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural 'them' and the time limit for eating show separate pieces, not one pressed mass.

steps.title: The crumbs came from a large loaf
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: the ברייתא is about crumbs that broke off a large loaf of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are we dealing with here? Crumbs that came from a large loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first answer and gives a new one. The ברייתא is talking about crumbs that broke off a big loaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer keeps the crumbs as separate pieces, so the plural wording fits. It still limits the ברייתא to a special case, crumbs from a large loaf. So the ברייתא does not prove that every small crumb counts as bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the previous answer and offers a new one.
A large loaf of bread.

phrases.english: Rather, here, what are we dealing with?
Where it came from a large loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 15 with a new one that fits the wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new limiting of the ברייתא to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that any loose crumbs count as bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about crumbs from a large loaf.

steps.title: Final ruling: even small crumbs get המוציא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the final ruling. רב ששת says even crumbs smaller than a כזית get המוציא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it? רב ששת said: even crumbs that are not the size of a כזית get המוציא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the final הלכה is on the ברכה for small pieces of bread. רב ששת rules that even crumbs smaller than a כזית get המוציא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said in step 11 that pieces smaller than a כזית get בורא מיני מזונות. רב ששת disagrees. He says size is not what decides the ברכה, so even small crumbs get המוציא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it? It asks for the final ruling.
Crumbs or small pieces.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for the ברכה on small pieces of bread.

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?
Rav Sheshet said:
Even crumbs that do not have an olive-bulk.
phrases.notes: The words 'get המוציא' are left out but assumed; this is the ברכה question from step 11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the back-and-forth over the ברייתא and asks for the final הלכה on the ruling of step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even crumbs smaller than a כזית get המוציא.

steps.title: Only if the crumbs still look like bread
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits רב ששת's ruling: the crumbs must still look like bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: and this is only when they still have the look of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a condition to רב ששת's ruling. Small crumbs get המוציא only if they still look like bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Size does not matter, but appearance does. If the crumbs have dissolved in the cooked dish and no longer look like bread, they lose the ברכה of bread.

keyTerms.meaning: The look or appearance of something.
Bread (Aramaic).

steps.whatToRemember: Small crumbs, even less than a כזית, get המוציא as long as they still look like bread (רב ששת with רבא's condition).

phrases.english: Rava said:
And this is where there is the appearance
of bread on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְהוּא דְּאִיכָּא תּוֹרִיתָא דְּנַהְמָא עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to רב ששת's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Crumbs get המוציא only when they still look like bread.
